messages:
maria: Heads up — we just saw a QPS drift on inference-proxy that spiked the external HPA metric. CA started adding GPU nodes and we ended up with an extra 12 g4dn nodes in us-west1. Cost alarm just fired. 😬
ashok: Oof. Which HPA metric is this wired to? external/prometheus_queue_length? Can you paste `kubectl get hpa`?
maria: Yep, external metric from prometheus-adapter. Here: ```
$ kubectl get hpa inference-workers -o yaml
metrics:
- type: External
  external:
    metricName: inference_queue_length
    target:
      type: AverageValue
      averageValue: "50"
behavior:
  scaleUp:
    stabilizationWindowSeconds: 0
    policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 200
        periodSeconds: 60
```
leo: The prometheus adapter has a scrapes -> query -> adapter lag. If prometheus scrapes every 30s and adapter aggregation is naive we can get spikes. Also CA sees pending pods and keeps scaling because HPA metric still > threshold while nodes provision.
sophia: Two quick mitigations: 1) set stabilizationWindowSeconds for scaleUp to ~60-120s to avoid reacting to transient spikes; 2) add a resource (CPU) metric as a secondary metric so pods can fall back if external metric is noisy.
jia: Also consider a small pre-warmed GPU nodepool with taint:gpu-warm=true and a toleration in the deployment. That avoids cold start provisioning delays that amplify autoscaler churn. Tradeoff is baseline cost but saves surge churn.
maria: Agree on warm-pool. Short term we need to stop more nodes from coming up — can we throttle CA?
ashok: You can set cluster-autoscaler flag `--max-node-provision-time` but that's global. Quick stop: scale down HPA `maxReplicas` to a safer cap (kubectl patch hpa) and rollback the external metric to a higher threshold. Doing that now.
ops-bot: Incident alert: cost-spike-us-west1 triggered at 1767778952. Current extra GPU hours estimate: ~45h.
leo: Longer term: change the prometheus query to use `avg_over_time()` sliding window and feed that to the adapter, or use a buffered queue-length metric emitted by the service (rate-limited). That smooths bursts.
sophia: Also tune CA settings: `--scale-down-unneeded-time` and `--scale-down-unready-time` to avoid flip-flopping, and enable `balance-similar-node-groups` so we don't concentrate scale actions in a single pool.
jia: Note region constraint: us-west1 has limited on-demand GPU capacity this week. If we keep spinning up nodes CA will fallback to next zone which is more expensive. Consider `nodeSelector` to prefer dedicated reserved pool if available.
maria: Patch applied: capped hpa maxReplicas=30 (was 80) and bumped external metric target to 80. Rolling back after traffic cools.
ashok: Follow-ups: 1) create gpu-warm-pool with taint + autoscaler min 1; 2) update prometheus-adapter query to avg_over_time(..[1m]); 3) add HPA stabilizationWindowSeconds=90 and add CPU fallback metric.
leo: I'll open a PR for the adapter query and HPA behavior change.
sophia: I'll draft infra ticket for warm pool sizing and cost trade analysis.
ops-bot: ack — created ticket INFRA-3271 for warm pool evaluation.
kube-adapter-bot: prometheus-adapter metrics now show 1m avg for inference_queue_length (deployed canary). Monitor for 10m.
maria: Thanks all — watching costs and queue now. Will update in 15m. :thumbsup:
